warning: Red: the DNR-flagged wildlife sanctuary WMAs (closed to hunting, trapping, fishing and trespass in their posted parts from Sept 1 through the last day of the duck season), the Red Lake Band lands (closed to non-members) and 1.5 miles of MN-62 at Talcot Lake. Amber: special rules: the designated hunting stations at Lac qui Parle, Talcot Lake, Roseau River, Thief Lake and Orwell, motorized-boat limits on the DNR feeding and resting lakes, Nett Lake, the early-teal restrictions on three reservations and the open-water lakes. Outlines marked approximate are whole WMAs, reservations or lakes: the posted refuge or rule area is only part of it, so follow the signs. Not drawn: the other state game refuges (booklet table, p. 114-117), Mississippi River open-water stretches and Lake Superior, county and city rules, and the trolling-motor and airboat lake lists beyond the DNR layer. Always check the current regulations.

Lac qui Parle Game Refuge (Chippewa and Lac qui Parle counties, 2026 regulations p. 46 and 113): waterfowl hunting only at designated first-come hunting stations from October 17 (p. 46; p. 113 prints October 19: confirm with the DNR) through the end of the goose season; the posted sanctuary parts, the state park and the Mission Site are closed to hunting. APPROXIMATE: outline of the WMA refuge unit.

Talcot Lake Game Refuge (Cottonwood County, p. 46 and 114): open to waterfowl hunting at designated stations only during the regular goose season; the Talcot Lake Waterfowl Refuge inside it is closed to waterfowl hunting except for persons with disabilities hunting geese at designated stations. APPROXIMATE: outline of the WMA.

Roseau River WMA (controlled hunting zone, p. 46): designated hunting stations, first come first served, no occupying or parking in a station from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m., no alcohol at stations. APPROXIMATE: outline of the WMA.

Thief Lake WMA (controlled hunting zone, p. 46): designated hunting stations, first come first served, no occupying or parking in a station from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m., no alcohol at stations; motors limited to 10 horsepower (p. 113). APPROXIMATE: outline of the WMA.

Orwell (controlled hunting zone, p. 46): designated hunting stations, first come first served, no occupying or parking in a station from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m., no alcohol at stations. APPROXIMATE: outline of the WMA (a posted sanctuary part of it is also flagged by the DNR).

areas.n: Talcot Lake - MN-62 south of the waterfowl refuge
areas.d: All waterfowl hunting is prohibited upon or from the 1.5 miles of Minnesota Highway 62 and its right-of-way along the south boundary of the Talcot Lake Waterfowl Refuge, between the Cottonwood County line on the west and County Highway 7 on the east (2026 regulations, p. 46). APPROXIMATE: a locator circle at the south edge of Talcot Lake WMA; the closed strip runs along the road.

areas.n: Red Lake Reservation - closed to non-members
areas.d: Lands of the Red Lake Band of Ojibwe in Beltrami, Koochiching, Lake of the Woods and Roseau counties are closed to non-band members except by special authorization of the tribal council (2026 regulations p. 127). APPROXIMATE: the outline is the Census reservation boundary (it includes Upper and Lower Red Lake); the Northwest Angle is not part of it.

areas.n: Mille Lacs Reservation - early teal restriction
areas.d: Early teal season (September 5-9 only; 2026 regulations p. 48): within the Mille Lacs Reservation, the taking of teal is prohibited on wild rice waters identified by the tribal authorities. Contact Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe (millelacsband.com or 320-532-7896). APPROXIMATE: the outline is the Census reservation boundary; only the wild-rice waters are affected.

areas.n: Leech Lake Reservation - early teal restriction
areas.d: Early teal season (September 5-9 only; 2026 regulations p. 48): within the Leech Lake Reservation, the taking of teal is prohibited within half a mile of wild rice beds posted open to rice harvest by the tribal authorities. Contact Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe (llojibwe.org/drm or 218-368-4767). APPROXIMATE: the outline is the Census reservation boundary; only the wild-rice waters are affected.

areas.n: White Earth Reservation - early teal restriction
areas.d: Early teal season (September 5-9 only; 2026 regulations p. 48): within the White Earth Reservation, the taking of teal is prohibited on wild rice waters identified by the tribal authorities. Contact White Earth Nation (whiteearth.com or 218-935-3933). APPROXIMATE: the outline is the Census reservation boundary; only the wild-rice waters are affected.

areas.n: Nett Lake - closed to non-band hunters
areas.d: Nett Lake (Koochiching and St. Louis counties) is closed to hunting by non-band members, except for duck hunting when accompanied by a band-member guide (2026 regulations p. 127). Outline: USGS NHD lake; the Bois Forte lands around it are not mapped.

areas.n: Lake of the Woods - open-water hunting allowed
areas.d: Open-water hunting is allowed from anchored boats on Lake of the Woods (2026 regulations p. 41-42). Elsewhere the open-water rule applies: no taking in open water unless concealed by natural vegetation, on a river or stream not over 100 yards wide, or pursuing wounded birds. Outline: USGS NHD.

Open-water hunting is allowed from anchored boats on Lake Mille Lacs (2026 regulations p. 42). Parts of it lie within the Mille Lacs Reservation (early-teal restriction on wild-rice waters). Outline: USGS NHD.
Open-water hunting is allowed from anchored boats on Lake Pepin (2026 regulations p. 42). The lake is shared with Wisconsin; the outline is the whole lake (NHD). Outline: USGS NHD.
